situation: A major automotive OEM's quality-escape rate and internal waste were high enough in the late 1990s to threaten customer satisfaction and warranty cost, prompting a company-wide Six Sigma program ("Consumer-Driven Six Sigma").
diagnosis: DMAIC-based root-cause analysis was applied across manufacturing and engineering processes; one documented example at the Saarlouis plant found a defective solvent-recovery valve was driving excessive paint use and VOC emissions.
action_taken: Replaced the failing valve with a stainless-steel design and adjusted the application process for certain paint steps; the wider program trained thousands of employees across roughly 10,000 improvement projects.
outcome: Widely and consistently reported (across multiple independent secondary sources) figures include a defect rate near 1 per 14.8 vehicles, ~$1 billion saved 2000-2002, and $2.19 billion in cumulative waste eliminated over the following decade — but these are secondary-sourced historical figures, not an independently audited primary report.
source_organization: Ford Motor Company — Consumer-Driven Six Sigma program (via SixSigma.us)

situation: An automotive car-parts supplier's die-casting and machining processes had a chronically high defect incidence rate undermining process capability.
diagnosis: Researchers applied DMAIC with design of experiments and hypothesis testing to isolate the main defect causes across both die-casting and machining operations, published as a peer-reviewed case study.
action_taken: Targeted corrective actions addressed the identified causal factors in both process steps.
outcome: Defect incidence fell from a chronically high level to an acceptable, sustained one, with process sigma level rising from 3.4σ to 4σ (peer-reviewed, published result).
source_organization: Condé, G.C.P.; Oprime, P.C.; Pimenta, M.L.; Sordan, J.E.; Bueno, C.R. — International Journal of Quality & Reliability Management, Vol. 40 No. 9 (2023)

situation: Quanta Computer, an electronics manufacturer of high-performance computing and telecommunications equipment, needed to strengthen workforce Lean competency to reduce waste and sustain continuous improvement.
diagnosis: Tennessee MEP's assessment identified a structured-Lean-skills gap (5S, value stream mapping, standard work, structured problem-solving) rather than a single equipment or process root cause.
action_taken: Tennessee MEP delivered a five-day on-site Lean Certificate Series combining classroom instruction, hands-on exercises, and real-world case-study analysis.
outcome: NIST MEP reports $145,000 in new/retained sales, $150,000 in new investment, and $200,000 in cost savings attributable to the engagement — self-reported by the company to the government program, not independently audited.
source_organization: NIST Manufacturing Extension Partnership — Tennessee MEP / Quanta Computer

situation: In the 1980s, Motorola's electronics/semiconductor manufacturing quality was falling behind Japanese competitors, with defect rates threatening its ability to compete.
diagnosis: Motorola engineer Bill Smith and colleagues developed the Six Sigma statistical quality methodology to drive process variation down to a documented, targeted defect level (3.4 defects per million opportunities) rather than relying on ad hoc fixes.
action_taken: Deployed Six Sigma training and DMAIC-style process discipline company-wide across electronics manufacturing operations, later publishing the methodology publicly.
outcome: Widely-cited historical figures report more than $16 billion in cumulative savings and up to 90-100% defect reductions in targeted processes over the following decade — a well-corroborated but secondary-sourced historical claim, not an independently audited figure reviewed directly here.
source_organization: Motorola Inc. — Six Sigma program history

situation: Microban International, a North Carolina manufacturer of antimicrobial polymer/plastic pellet compounds, developed a new formulation that burned during processing instead of blending invisibly into customers' clear polymer products, leaving visible black flecks in finished parts.
diagnosis: The defect traced to the compounding/formulation step, not a molding-parameter issue at the customer's press — isolating it required specialized compounding equipment Microban didn't have in-house.
action_taken: Partnered with the Polymers Center of Excellence (PCE), part of North Carolina's MEP, using PCE's dryers, compounding extruders, and high-precision feeders to test and refine the formulation.
outcome: Microban's director of materials engineering reported the refined material performed much better, and that for every dollar spent at PCE the company sees at least a tenfold return in new business generated — a self-reported ROI claim, not an independently audited figure.
source_organization: NIST Manufacturing Extension Partnership — NC Polymers Center of Excellence / Microban International

situation: A plastic manufacturing operation had long mold/tool/die changeover times constraining production capacity, documented as a published Six Sigma case study.
diagnosis: Six Sigma tools were applied to the changeover process specifically, separating and measuring the distinct steps contributing to total changeover duration — the same internal/external setup distinction SMED and Scientific Molding both use.
action_taken: Process changes targeting the highest-contributing changeover steps were implemented and measured against before/after run data.
outcome: The published paper reports a reduction in mold/tool/die changeover time; the specific percentage sits in the original paper and was not independently confirmed here — not reproduced without that confirmation.
source_organization: Kale, K. — "Process Improvement in a Plastic Manufacturing Industry using Six Sigma Tools," indexed via the International Society of Six Sigma Professionals (ISSSP)

situation: CJB Industries, a contract chemical manufacturer for agricultural and pest-control industries, had employees spending excessive time weekly manually processing non-standard printed batch sheets across 200+ diverse customers, limiting quality visibility and throughput.
diagnosis: Georgia MEP's assessment identified manual batch-sheet processing and a paper-based QMS as the binding constraints on quality (price of non-conformance) and capacity, not a process-parameter issue on the manufacturing line itself.
action_taken: Implemented dataPARC real-time process-data analytics, deployed a new QMS replacing the paper-based one, and partnered with an AI vendor to convert printed batch sheets into standardized digital workflows.
outcome: NIST MEP reports a 51% reduction in price of non-conformance (PONC), a 20% increase in production capacity, and $30,000/month in preventive-maintenance savings against a $300,000 technology investment — self-reported to the government program, not independently audited.
source_organization: NIST Manufacturing Extension Partnership — Georgia MEP / CJB Industries

situation: Isotec International, a chemical manufacturer serving automotive, taxidermy, and other industries, needed to strengthen staff/management communication to manage growth as order volume increased.
diagnosis: Georgia MEP's Managing for Daily Improvement (MDI) assessment identified a daily-communication and KPI-visibility gap — raw-material issues and priority information weren't reaching the right people in time — rather than a capacity or equipment constraint.
action_taken: Implemented MDI training: identifying critical metrics, developing KPIs, and running 30-minute daily GEMBA walks throughout the plant for real-time problem-solving.
outcome: NIST MEP reports a 43% revenue increase, 90% increase in new customer acquisition, 50% reduction in approval time, and a 75% improvement in daily raw-material issue communication — self-reported to the government program, not independently audited.
source_organization: NIST Manufacturing Extension Partnership — Georgia MEP / Isotec International

situation: A pharmaceutical manufacturer's production flow carried excess work-in-process and long cycle times typical of a push-scheduled, batch-oriented operation.
diagnosis: Researchers documented the operation's flow and applied Lean management principles to re-engineer production sequencing, published as a peer-reviewed case study of Lean adoption specifically in a regulated pharmaceutical environment.
action_taken: Re-engineered the production flow around a pull-based scheduling system rather than the prior push-based approach.
outcome: The published paper reports improvement across efficiency KPIs, work-in-process, and cycle time; the specific percentages sit behind the journal's access wall and were not independently confirmed here — not reproduced without that confirmation.
source_organization: Nenni, M.E.; Giustiniano, L.; Pirolo, L. — published case study on Lean management in the pharmaceutical industry (2014)

situation: A large multinational pharmaceutical organization had a significant backlog of open deviations and CAPAs, requiring a broader quality management system remediation effort.
diagnosis: The backlog itself — not any single deviation's root cause — was identified as the primary quality-system risk, since a growing backlog delays closure on every open item and compounds audit exposure.
action_taken: Engaged specialized QA staff augmentation for deviation/CAPA backlog remediation and quality-system corrective work, starting as a fixed-term engagement later extended for continuity.
outcome: The publicly available material describes the engagement evolving into ongoing augmented QA leadership roles, but does not include specific quantified backlog-reduction figures — an honest gap in the source, not a magnitude claim omitted here.
source_organization: The FDA Group — pharmaceutical QA staff augmentation case study

situation: A home appliance manufacturer's aluminum casting department had a high leakage-type defect rate in aluminum components.
diagnosis: A DMAIC Six Sigma study used design of experiments and regression analysis to identify aluminum molten-metal temperature as the key variable correlated with defect occurrence.
action_taken: Adjusted the process to the optimized aluminum molten-metal temperature identified through the DOE/regression analysis.
outcome: Published results report the aluminum defect rate fell from 10.49% to 6.1%, with the Six Sigma level improving from 2.8 to 3.06 — a peer-reviewed, published figure.
source_organization: Ahmed, N.G.S.; Abohashima, H.S.; Aly, M.F. — Proceedings of the International Conference on Industrial Engineering and Operations Management, Washington DC (2018)

situation: Whirlpool's Duet washer/dryer product line needed a design-quality improvement process reflecting how customers actually evaluate quality, not only internal engineering specs.
diagnosis: Whirlpool's Six Sigma team identified a gap between engineering-defined and customer-perceived quality metrics as the structural issue behind the design/quality disconnect.
action_taken: Applied Six Sigma design-process discipline to develop new quality metrics aligned with customer evaluation criteria, integrated into the Duet design process.
outcome: Reported as a notable Six Sigma design-for-quality case in consumer appliances in secondary Six Sigma industry sources; no specific defect-rate or return-rate figures were found in the sources reviewed — treat only the directional claim as reported, not any magnitude.
source_organization: Whirlpool Corporation — Six Sigma Duet product design case (as reported via Six Sigma industry secondary sources)

situation: Keats Manufacturing Company, a custom metal stampings/wire-forms/assemblies manufacturer, had hydraulic punch presses with no system to measure machine availability, performance, or quality — making it impossible to accurately calculate production capacity or identify operational losses.
diagnosis: TMAC (the regional MEP center) determined the root gap was measurement infrastructure itself — OEE couldn't be improved because it couldn't be reliably measured in the first place.
action_taken: Designed and installed an embedded OEE-measurement system using Arduino microcontrollers with optical and electrical-current sensors to automatically collect cycle counts, availability data, and defect counts.
outcome: Keats reports increased measurement accuracy and the ability to plan maintenance proactively; NIST MEP's own published summary explicitly states a dollar-savings figure "has not been developed" yet, describing savings only as "inevitable" — an honest gap in the source, not an outcome claimed here.
source_organization: NIST Manufacturing Extension Partnership — TMAC / Keats Manufacturing Company

situation: A mid-scale industrial manufacturing facility (anonymized by the publishing vendor) had frequent equipment breakdowns, inconsistent maintenance practices, and rising operational costs, running a time-based (not condition-based) maintenance program that ignored asset criticality.
diagnosis: A risk-based asset-management consultancy assessment attributed the breakdown pattern to the maintenance strategy itself — treating all assets the same regardless of criticality or condition — rather than to any single equipment failure mode.
action_taken: Implemented a structured ISO 55001-aligned asset management system: a verified asset register, criticality assessment, and risk-based/condition-based maintenance planning replacing the prior time-based schedule.
outcome: Reported over one operating year: downtime reduced ~15% (62 to 43 hrs/month), preventive-maintenance compliance improved from 68% to 86%, and high-risk asset failures fell from 11 to 4 incidents — the client is anonymized by the vendor publishing the case study, so this cannot be independently cross-checked.
source_organization: 4CPL — "Risk-Based Asset Management with ISO 55001" case study (anonymized client)
